nodes.summary: For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a natural number $k$, $\mathrm{AP}_k(A)$ is the number of pairs $(a, d)$ of natural numbers with $a \in A$ and $1 \le d \le \max A$ such that $a + i d \in A$ for every natural number $i < k$. For $k \ge 2$ the conditions $a \in A$ and $d \le \max A$ follow from the others, so $\mathrm{AP}_k(A)$ counts the $k$-term progressions $a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1) d$ in $A$…

nodes.title: The progression threshold $F_k(N, \ell)$

nodes.summary: A finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains a $k$-term arithmetic progression when there are natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ with $a + i d \in A$ for every natural number $i < k$, that is, $a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1) d$ all lie in $A$. For $k = 0$ this holds vacuously.
nodes.title: Containing a $k$-term arithmetic progression

nodes.summary: For every natural number $\ell > 3$, $\log F_3(N, \ell) / \log N \to 2$ as $N \to \infty$ over the natural numbers, where $F_3(N, \ell)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that every $N$-element set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ containing at least $m$ three-term arithmetic progressions $a, a + d, a + 2d$ with $d \ge 1$ contains an $\ell$-term arithmetic progression.
